title: Read the thumbnail index once in the direct image scan
head: 036cd3411321
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A writer-produced filename with consecutive tabs can hide a different image's cached thumbnail
leads.consequence: The writer prints unescaped filenames into index.tsv. Given an indexed filename picture.png<TAB><TAB><size:mtime of picture.png><TAB>shadow.png, Bash IFS collapses the consecutive tabs and inserts a spurious key for picture.png with hash shadow.png. Because the map keeps its first entry, the later genuine picture.png record is ignored; the direct picker shows the source image instead of its existing thumbnail on every scan until the offending index row is removed. The old awk lookup ignores the malformed first record and uses the later genuine one. This does not require editing the index by hand, though a specially named image and a matching size:mtime field are needed. Preserve empty TSV columns (do not use tab as IFS whitespace for these records) or validate raw rows before insertion.

leads.summary: Every one-image scan now loads the entire unbounded index even if the match is first
leads.consequence: The writer only appends rows; a picker with one image and a first-row cache hit used to exit awk immediately, but now iterates and allocates a Bash array for all stale entries on every direct scan. With 100,000 stale synthetic records and one matched image the isolated C-locale runs took 0.562s on the head versus 0.007s on the base, and both returned the same cached thumbnail. Longer-lived caches or multiple direct opens amplify the delay (the QML scan waits for stdout to finish). Consider using the indexed bulk pass only above a threshold of images, or build only the keys required by the current image set, with a fast path for a tiny image list.

leads.summary: The new test passes even if the implementation never reads the index
leads.consequence: The sole seeded indexed hash is exactly the md5 that thumbnail_path_for computes when lookup fails, and two.png is intentionally unindexed. Replacing the new index loader's condition with 'if false; then' leaves every assertion green, including the zero-awk check. An additional plausible mutant that stops reading after the first row also passes because the only other row is a duplicate. The test reliably fails against the old per-image awk implementation but cannot detect a missing bulk loader or truncated reads. Give one.png a valid cached hash distinct from the md5 fallback and add a second distinct indexed image whose cached path is asserted.

leads.summary: An empty hash row no longer blocks later duplicates, and an empty hash plus extra column becomes a spurious hash
leads.consequence: For a manually edited or damaged row with the right path and signature but an empty hash, awk exits after printing an empty value, so the old picker uses its md5 fallback. The new loop skips that row and takes a later duplicate with a different hash. If an extra column follows an empty hash, IFS splitting shifts it into the hash variable; the picker may select that wrong thumbnail. These formats are not emitted by the normal writer with ordinary filenames, so this is a malformed-index compatibility issue, separate from the producer-backed tab collision in P1. Preserve field positions and mark the first matching row even when its hash is empty.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Q1 malformed rows), writer does not produce

leads.summary: A final complete index record without a newline is discarded
leads.consequence: Bash read assigns the last record but returns nonzero at EOF without a newline, so the while body never inserts that key. Awk used the last record. In an index with a non-md5 cached hash (for instance a manually populated one), a cache hit becomes a fallback to the original image on every scan. The current writer normally appends a newline and its usual hash equals the fallback, so a normally completed writer-produced last row does not change the visible thumbnail; this matters for imported/custom or interrupted records where a different cache file exists. Process a nonempty unterminated final record with 'read -r ... || [[ -n ... ]]' while handling empty fields.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Q1 missing final newline)

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** For a few images, the new loader is slower than the old `awk` scans once the index grows.

### Few-image scans slow down as the index grows

The bash `read` loop costs about 9 µs per index row, against about 1 µs for an `awk` scan. With a few thousand rows, it only wins from about ten images. **Impact:** the direct scan's default directory, theme backgrounds (2 to 9 in stock themes), slows as the unpruned index grows: 39 ms at base, 163 ms at head, for 3 images and 20,000 rows.

**Suggested change:** Do the single pass in `awk`, passing bash only the scanned images' rows (sketch in Details).

<details><summary>Reproducer (slower at 036cd34)</summary>

An upstream clone needs `git fetch origin pull/13568/head` first.

Self-contained. Save the script below as `repro-perf.sh`, then from an omarchy checkout:

```bash
git show b18ab4952b88:shell/plugins/image-picker/list.sh >list-base.sh
git show 036cd3411321:shell/plugins/image-picker/list.sh >list-head.sh
bash repro-perf.sh list-base.sh list-head.sh
```

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Usage: repro-perf.sh OLD_LIST_SH NEW_LIST_SH
# Times the direct scan of a three-image directory against thumbnail indexes
# of growing size (median of five runs each).
set -euo pipefail
old=$1 new=$2
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
images="$tmp/images"
cache="$tmp/cache"
sel="$cache/omarchy/image-selector"
mkdir -p "$images" "$sel"
for i in 1 2 3; do printf 'image %d' "$i" >"$images/$i.jpg"; done

for rows in 1000 5000 20000; do
  awk -v m="$rows" 'BEGIN { for (i = 0; i < m; i++) printf "/old/theme/backgrounds/%d.jpg\t%d:%d\t%032x\n", i % 7, 100000 + i, 1700000000 + i, i }' >"$sel/index.tsv"
  for f in "$images"/*; do
    sig=$(stat -Lc '%s:%Y' "$f")
    h=$(printf '%s\t%s' "$f" "$sig" | md5sum | cut -d ' ' -f 1)
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$f" "$sig" "$h" >>"$sel/index.tsv"
    : >"$sel/$h.jpg"
  done
  for script in "$old" "$new"; do
    times=()
    for run in 1 2 3 4 5; do
      start=$EPOCHREALTIME
      XDG_CACHE_HOME="$cache" bash "$script" "$images" >/dev/null
      times+=("$(awk -v s="$start" -v e="$EPOCHREALTIME" 'BEGIN { printf "%.0f", (e - s) * 1000 }')")
    done
    printf '%6d index rows, 3 images  %-17s %4s ms\n' "$rows" "${script##*/}" "$(printf '%s\n' "${times[@]}" | sort -n | sed -n 3p)"
  done
done
```

Actual output (GNU bash 5.3.15, GNU Awk 5.4.1, 16 CPUs, run inside an isolated sandbox):

```
  1000 index rows, 3 images  list-base.sh        17 ms
  1000 index rows, 3 images  list-head.sh        21 ms
  5000 index rows, 3 images  list-base.sh        19 ms
  5000 index rows, 3 images  list-head.sh        57 ms
 20000 index rows, 3 images  list-base.sh        39 ms
 20000 index rows, 3 images  list-head.sh       163 ms
```
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

The same script with `list-head.sh` replaced by a variant whose loader is one awk pass over the index that keeps only rows for the scanned images (first row per key), each pair run back to back:

```
  1000 index rows, 3 images  list-base.sh        14 ms
  1000 index rows, 3 images  list-awk-pass.sh    11 ms
  5000 index rows, 3 images  list-base.sh        21 ms
  5000 index rows, 3 images  list-awk-pass.sh    14 ms
 20000 index rows, 3 images  list-base.sh        39 ms
 20000 index rows, 3 images  list-awk-pass.sh    20 ms
```

The variant's loader, replacing the `declare -A thumbnail_index=()` ... `fi` block (relies on GNU awk for the NUL record separator, which is Arch's `awk`):

```bash
declare -A thumbnail_index=()
if [[ -f $index_file ]] && (( ${#images[@]} > 0 )); then
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r -d '' path signature hash; do
    thumbnail_index["$path"$'\t'"$signature"]=$hash
  done < <(printf '%s\0' "${images[@]}" | awk -F '\t' '
    FNR == NR { want[$0]; next }
    ($1 in want) && !(($1 FS $2) in seen) { seen[$1 FS $2]; if ($3 != "") printf "%s\t%s\t%s%c", $1, $2, $3, 0 }
  ' RS='\0' - RS='\n' "$index_file" 2>/dev/null)
fi
```

- Adding `$2 != ""` to the `awk` condition keeps base parsing for rows with an empty field. That guarded form was checked for output only, not timed.
- With the sketch, the new test's zero-`awk` assertion would become `(( $(wc -l <"$awk_calls") <= 1 ))`.
- Median of 5 runs: with 50 images, the head is faster from 1,000 rows up (100 ms against 201 ms at 1,000 rows). With 0 unrelated rows, the head is faster at every size.
</details>

### The new test passes when the index is never read

The seeded `one_hash` equals the md5 fallback, so the check passes even when the lookup misses. **Impact:** 4 of 5 mutants that break the lookup still pass.

**Suggested change:** Seed a non-fallback hash, such as `one_hash=$(printf 'indexed' | md5sum | cut -d ' ' -f 1)`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (passes with the loader broken, at 036cd34)</summary>

From the root of a checkout at the PR head (036cd341). The first command deletes the line that stores index rows, so every lookup falls back to the md5 name; the PR's test still passes, because the hash it seeds is exactly that md5 fallback. Changing the seeded hash to one the fallback would not produce makes the test fail on the broken script and pass on the unmodified one.

Actual transcript (run inside an isolated sandbox on a copy of the head files; the temporary path is shortened to `<tmp>`):

```
$ sed -i '/^    thumbnail_index\[.*\]=\$hash$/d' shell/plugins/image-picker/list.sh
[exit 0]

$ diff -u <before> shell/plugins/image-picker/list.sh
@@ -106,7 +106,6 @@
   while IFS=$'\t' read -r path signature hash _; do
     [[ -n $path && -n $signature && -n $hash ]] || continue
     [[ -z ${thumbnail_index["$path"$'\t'"$signature"]-} ]] || continue
-    thumbnail_index["$path"$'\t'"$signature"]=$hash
   done <"$index_file" 2>/dev/null
 fi
 

$ bash test/shell.d/image-picker-list-test.sh
ok - direct picker reads the thumbnail index once and keeps first-row lookups
[exit 0]

$ sed -i "s/^one_hash=.*/one_hash=\$(printf 'indexed' | md5sum | cut -d ' ' -f 1)/" test/shell.d/image-picker-list-test.sh
[exit 0]

$ diff -u <before> test/shell.d/image-picker-list-test.sh
@@ -27,7 +27,7 @@
 mkdir -p "$cache_dir"
 
 one_signature=$(stat -Lc '%s:%Y' "$images/one.png")
-one_hash=$(printf '%s\t%s' "$images/one.png" "$one_signature" | md5sum | cut -d ' ' -f 1)
+one_hash=$(printf 'indexed' | md5sum | cut -d ' ' -f 1)
 duplicate_hash=$(printf 'duplicate' | md5sum | cut -d ' ' -f 1)
 printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$images/one.png" "$one_signature" "$one_hash" >>"$cache_dir/index.tsv"
 # A later duplicate row must not change the answer a lookup gets.

$ bash test/shell.d/image-picker-list-test.sh
<tmp>/images/one.png
not ok - direct picker reuses the indexed thumbnail for a scanned image
[exit 1]

$ bash test/shell.d/image-picker-list-test.sh   # unmutated list.sh, changed test
ok - direct picker reads the thumbnail index once and keeps first-row lookups
[exit 0]

```

Other ways of breaking the lookup, run against both test versions in a separate harness: keying stored rows with a space instead of a tab, making `thumbnail_path_for` ignore the array, and skipping the loader entirely all pass the PR's test and fail the changed one. Letting a later duplicate row win fails both versions.
</details>

<details><summary>Optional notes</summary>

- `done <"$index_file" 2>/dev/null` opens the file before stderr is silenced, so an unreadable index now prints `Permission denied`. `done 2>/dev/null <"$index_file"` keeps the old quiet behaviour.
- `read` treats a run of tabs as one separator, where `awk -F '\t'` keeps the empty fields. It also drops a last row with no final newline. The writer never produces these rows for ordinary file names. In the direct-scan picker, a crafted double-tab file name, indexed before the target image with the target's size and mtime known in advance, can make that image's tile show another cached preview. The base allows the same with a single tab. The `awk` sketch keeps the base behaviour here.
- `(( ${#images[@]} > 0 ))` instead of `-gt` inside `[[ ]]` would follow the style in AGENTS.md.
</details>

<details><summary>Verified</summary>

- With an index written by `omarchy-menu-images` for 16 file names, most of them unusual (spaces, tabs, brackets, quotes, backslashes, newlines), head and base print the same rows.
- The array is visible inside the video pass's command substitutions.
- The new test fails on the base with two `awk` calls and passes on the head. `image-picker-test.sh` and `menu-images-test.sh` pass.
- `video-background-test.sh` fails the same way at the base and at the head, on an unset `PREPARED_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT` in its theme section. The failure is unrelated to this PR.
</details>
